transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-13 15:00 PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marcus Reed (Valence VP Eng), Sana Iqbal (Valence Head ML Ops), Tomas Rojas (Valence Security)

Summary (auto-gen, imperfect): quick sync about next year's commit tiers, discuss eu-onprem pilot, go over latency vs cost tradeoffs, and identify security docs needed.

00:00 Jordan: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan Lee here from Redwood, with Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
00:05 Marcus: Good, thanks. Sorry for the slight delay, had a standup runover.
00:12 Jordan: No worries. Quick agenda — tiered uplift numbers, EU private pilot, latency fallback policy and security asks. If that sounds good we can dive in.
00:22 Sana: Sounds great, Marcus and I have some constraints to share up front — majorly latency for production inference (<120ms p95 for short prompts), and we have a security gating around KMS integration and audit logs.
00:35 Priya: Cool, that's helpful. When you say <120ms p95 is that for single-turn short prompts, or for the full chat flow?
00:42 Sana: Single-turn first-party prompts, ~32 tokens typical. Multi-turn baseline is longer but we care mostly about prompt latency that drives UI.
00:50 Priya: Ok, that helps. A couple quick qualifiers — are you leaning towards Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem)?
00:59 Marcus: For the EU pilot we want private — data residency. But for burst and dev traffic we might remain hosted in US until we ramp. So a hybrid approach.
01:09 Jordan: Understood. So the uplift that we discussed in the deck — the tiered retainer — would be a committed throughput with reserved GPUs and priority routing, then overflow to hosted. That gives a predictable unit cost but keeps headroom.
01:25 Marcus: Can you remind us the delta in unit cost if we commit to the 3-tier vs the 1-tier? I think it was non-linear.
01:33 Jordan: Yes — at a high level our 3-tier commitment (base, burst buffer, burst on-demand) drops per-token costs by ~28% compared to pure on-demand hosted. But actual savings depend on batching and quantization. Priya, want to take the perf numbers?
01:45 Priya: Sure. For the Mariner-7 model with typical 32-token prompts, on a c5-large GPU variant (quantized path) you'd see median latency ~60–80ms with continuous batching turned on; p95 can be kept under 120ms if we maintain small batch sizes and KV cache hit rates are high. If you push larger batch windows to save cost, p95 rises — that's the usual tradeoff.
02:10 Sana: When you say KV cache hit rate — are we talking prefix caching across sessions? Our chat app sends session IDs, we need session-level KV cache so repeated contexts hit.
02:19 Priya: Exactly, we can cache prefixes per session — Redwood's runtime supports prefix/KV caching, though initial cold start still pays the latency. Also if you pin a model version in Private, the warm cache behavior is more stable.
02:33 Tomas: On KMS — we run HashiCorp Vault in our EU cluster, we need Redwood Private to integrate with our KMS and provide audit log entries. Is that supported out of the box?
02:44 Jordan: We support customer-managed KMS (HSM or Vault) for Private. We'll need to exchange the integration checklist; there are a few ops steps but we've done similar integrations. Also audit logs can be exported to your S3 or SIEM in masked form.
02:58 Tomas: Masked form meaning PII removed? We need full traceability for admin actions.
03:06 Jordan: For admin audit logs we can provide full entries, for request/response payloads we practice redaction. We'll put the SOC2 appendix in the docs we share.
03:16 Marcus: Great. Back to latency: if we commit to Dedicated instead of Private, do we get better latency guarantees?
03:25 Priya: Dedicated gives predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools and tends to have lower jitter because of less noisy neighbors. Private adds network/ops overhead depending on VPC setup; you can still meet 120ms p95 but we'd need co-located hardware in EU and tuning.
03:39 Marcus: So for the EU pilot we'd likely do Private with local GPU nodes, and for US production we remain Dedicated. That means we need a cross-region fallback policy.
03:50 Jordan: Yeah, we can define smart routing: prefer EU private, fallback to EU hosted or US dedicated depending on rules. Fallbacks can be latency or cost-driven. We also support canary rules for rollouts.
04:02 Sana: One concern — fallbacks need to preserve data residency constraints. We can't route EU customer PII out of EU. How does Redwood enforce that?
04:12 Priya: Routing policies are policy-driven — you can tag requests and disallow routing out of region for certain request types. We'll map request attributes to route policies.
04:21 Tomas: Ok, but exception handling when EU capacity is saturated — what options? Queue? Reject? Send to a model variant that keeps data in EU but is lower capacity?
04:33 Priya: Options are: 1) automatic throttle / queue; 2) route to an EU-compatible lower-capacity model variant (quantized or smaller model) that you pin in the private cluster; 3) allow controlled overflow to hosted EU region (if contractual residency allows). We'll outline behaviors and you pick one.
04:50 Marcus: We probably prefer option 2 for critical PII flows. For non-PII we can fall back to US hosted.
04:58 Jordan: Makes sense. On the pricing piece — the tiered retainer we proposed includes a reserved base commit to cover most traffic plus a burst buffer. I will send a revised spreadsheet that breaks down per-token costs across three typical batching configs: aggressive batching (cost-opt), balanced (what we recommended), and low-latency (higher cost).
05:20 Marcus: Can you include a worked example based on our monthly 50M token usage with 70% short prompts?
05:27 Jordan: Absolutely — we'll model that.
05:30 Sana: There was also a question we forgot to ask — agent-based calls where we call external tools, does Redwood do function/tool calls isolation in Private? We want to ensure no third-party calls leak our secrets.
05:41 Priya: In Private, you control the network egress; you can disallow external HTTP calls or route them through your proxy. Tool calls are executed within your network boundary if you configure the connectors. That will be part of the onprem runbook.
05:54 Tomas: Good. Security questions — SSO/SCIM support? We need role-based access.
06:01 Jordan: Yes SSO (SAML/SCIM) and RBAC are supported. For Private you can integrate with your IdP; for hosted we have SCIM for user sync. We'll send the SSO integration guide.
06:12 Marcus: Ok would be good to see a sample access policy so our security team can review.
06:17 Jordan: We'll include a sample RBAC policy and sample audit log schema in the packet.
06:23 Sana: About benchmarks — we'd like Redwood to run a proof-of-performance for the EU pilot. What's the proposal?
06:30 Priya: We typically run a 2-hour benchmark window in a staging cluster with your representative prompts and traffic shape. For Private we can run in your staging VPC or in our EU staging if agreed. We need sample prompts, session patterns, and an auth token.
06:44 Marcus: We can provide a 30-minute set of prompts that reflect typical user journeys. We'll also want token-level cost numbers from that run.
06:52 Priya: Great. We'll also instrument KV cache warmups in the run so you can see p95 behavior over time.
07:00 Sana: Who will own the setup on the Redwood side?
07:03 Jordan: Priya will lead the technical run and coordinate with our infra team; I'll handle contractual pricing and legal redlines.
07:10 Priya: I'll need a staging endpoint, example payloads, and access to the KMS team for the Private test. 
07:18 Tomas: I'll set up an initial Connect ticket and share our Vault onboarding document.
07:22 Marcus: Ok, timeline wise — we'd like to lock the retainer in the next two weeks so procurement can start, while the EU pilot runs in early March. Is that realistic?
07:31 Jordan: Yes, we can aim to get pricing and security docs to you within 3 business days; the benchmark window can be scheduled for the week of March 3rd. We'll aim for contract start by March 15th if everything aligns.
07:44 Sana: A few nitty-gritty items — does Redwood support per-token attribution in billing? We have a need to attribute costs to product teams.
07:53 Jordan: Yes, token-level breakdown by route/model is available in Redwood Console; you can export CSVs and set cost centers.
07:59 Marcus: Competitor note — we also ran a quick comparison vs Anthropic's managed offering; their latency numbers were competitive for small prompts but cost was higher at scale. That influenced our thinking on a hybrid approach.
08:12 Jordan: Good datapoint. We'll include a simple comparison table in the follow-up.
08:17 Priya: Anything else on technical blockers?
08:20 Sana: One more: network egress costs for EU — do you pass through customer egress or is it included in the Private pricing?
08:28 Jordan: For Private, network egress is customer-controlled and billed by your infra. For Dedicated/hosted, we include outbound costs up to contractual limits; we'll call that out in the spreadsheet.
08:40 Marcus: Ok. Let's do a quick recap of agreed items.
08:44 Jordan: Recap: 1) Jordan will send revised tiered pricing and cost model with a worked example for 50M tokens (due 2025-02-18). 2) Priya to schedule and run a 2-hour benchmark window in staging (proposed week of 2025-03-03; setup items by 2025-02-20). 3) Sana/Tomas to share KMS and Vault onboarding docs and confirm compliance stakeholders (due 2025-02-16). 4) Redwood to share SOC2 appendix, SSO integration guide and RBAC sample (by 2025-02-16). 5) Define fallback policy: Valence prefers EU-local variant fallback for PII flows and US host fallback for non-PII — we'll formalize in runbook.
09:30 Marcus: That aligns. We'll review the pricing and aim to circle back before the weekend.
09:36 Jordan: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet and the spreadsheet.
09:41 Tomas: Thanks all.
09:43 (meeting ends)
